tasks.short: Watch equipment and material while working, check material against its certificate, report faults to the supervisor, fill in a non-conformance and let the supervisor decide.

steps.what: Welder watches the welding equipment and material for faulty operation during work
Welder checks plate heat numbers against the paper material certificate
Welder walks to find the supervisor to notify supervisors of the problem
Welder fills in a paper non-conformance form for defective materials
Production supervisor decides on repair, scrap or carrying on

tasks.design: The work order on the workstation tablet in the shop-floor module of the {ERP} shows the material certificate linked to each batch, and a fault button sends the supervisor a message with a photo and pre-filled non-conformance fields. Watching the work and the supervisor's decision stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates were paper in the office, and faults were reported by walking and on paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop-floor apps collect machine states and manual entries at the workplace.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting a fault is skill; a button does not help if no one sees the problem.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from the arc that something is wrong with the material.

reach.learn: Whether photo reports speed up decisions.

evidence.claim: Shop-floor monitoring collects quantities and machine states from the machine control or by manual entry and assigns them to the workplace.
Data tied to an operator login can observe performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing a fault to the supervisor's decision; repairs are outside.
Input contract: material certificates scanned and linked to batches by goods receipt; non-conformance fields set by the quality inspector; fallback is paper.
Supervisor time is outside the welder's savings.
Reports are per workstation, not used to judge welders.
unknowns: Whether tablets are at each workstation.
research_questions: Does time from fault to decision fall with fault messages?

incremental.description: Welder learns the fault button and photo.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Shops where the supervisor is always on the floor save little walking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read material and thickness from the drawing, look up the welding chart, fetch filler and flux, install torch and tip, and note the filler batch.

steps.what: Welder reads types and thicknesses of metals from the drawing
Welder looks up torch tips, filler rods and flux in the paper welding chart binder
Welder fetches filler rods and flux from the store
Welder selects and installs torches and torch tips and sets up the equipment
Welder writes the filler batch number on the job card

tasks.design: The welding procedure that applies to the part is linked to the work order and shows on the workstation tablet in the shop-floor module of the {ERP}, with tip size, filler, flux and settings, instead of searching the binder. The filler batch is scanned from its label onto the work order; fetching, fitting and setting up stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts and procedures were paper binders; batch numbers were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Welding data systems record welds per seam and component and pass data to the ERP.
tasks.still_hard: Procedures must be linked to every part; old parts may have none.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that this batch of plate welds differently from the last.

reach.task: Keep welding procedures linked to parts
reach.learn: Whether linked procedures cut wrong consumable choices.

evidence.claim: A welding data system records welding data per seam and component and passes it to MES or ERP.
Structural steel work requires welding to qualified procedures with traceable consumables.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading the drawing to the filler batch recorded; welding itself is outside.
Input contract: welding procedures written and linked to parts by the welding coordinator; consumable labels with batch barcodes from the supplier; fallback is the binder.
Coordinator time is outside the welder's savings.
Fetching and setting up do not change.
unknowns: Share of parts with linked procedures.
research_questions: Do wrong consumable choices fall after linking?

incremental.description: Welder learns the procedure view and batch scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Experienced welders on repeat parts seldom open the chart.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study the drawing and material, choose process, preheat and sequence, find a qualified procedure, work out joint geometry and ask the coordinator when nothing fits.

steps.what: Welder studies the drawing, joint types and material
Welder searches the procedure binder for a qualified procedure that covers the joint
Welder determines required equipment and welding methods, preheat and sequence from metallurgy and technique
Welder works out bevel geometry, root gap and number of passes by hand
Welder asks the welding coordinator when no procedure fits

tasks.design: The register of qualified welding procedures in {DOCS} is filtered by material group, thickness range, joint type and position, so the welder finds the covering procedure at once; a joint calculator gives bevel, gap and pass count for the chosen procedure for the welder to check. Choosing methods, preheat and sequence stay with the welder and the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were in a binder sorted by number, and geometry was worked out with tables.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable procedure registers and weld calculators are standard software.
tasks.still_hard: Metallurgy and distortion control need experience; filters only find what was qualified.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a sequence that keeps a long beam straight.

reach.learn: Whether a filtered register cuts questions.

evidence.claim: Weld calculators compute joint geometry and pass counts from standard formulas.
Structural welding must follow qualified procedures within their ranges.

assumptions: Boundary: from the drawing to the welding plan; qualifying new procedures is outside.
Input contract: procedure register with ranges kept by the welding coordinator; fallback is the binder.
Coordinator time is outside the welder's savings.
Judging methods and sequence does not change.
unknowns: Number of procedures in the register.
research_questions: How often does a filter return no covering procedure?

incremental.description: Welder learns the register filter and calculator.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Shops with few procedures find them quickly already.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the weld pool, check interpass temperature, measure and correct distortion, and record parameters and temperatures per seam.

steps.what: Welder watches the weld pool and arc during fitting, burning and welding processes
Welder checks interpass temperature to avoid overheating of parts
Welder measures warping and distortion and adjusts clamping or sequence
Welder writes parameters and interpass temperatures per seam on the paper weld record

tasks.design: The welding power source records current, voltage and wire speed per seam and component and passes them to the shop-floor module of the {ERP}; the welder adds only interpass temperatures on the tablet. Watching, measuring and correcting distortion stay with the welder.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parameters were read off the machine and written on paper records.
tasks.enabler_now: Welding data systems record data per seam and component and give reports at the touch of a button.
tasks.still_hard: Data tied to a welder ID can observe performance; parameters within limits do not prove a sound weld.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the plate start to pull and changing the sequence in time.

reach.learn: Whether recorded parameters cut inspection time.

evidence.claim: A welding data system records welding data per seam and component, gives reports at the touch of a button and passes data to MES or ERP.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: one weld from start to record; inspection is outside.

Input contract: seam and component ids from the work order; parameter limits from the welding procedure; power source data through the machine link set up by the maintenance engineer; fallback is the paper record.
Data are used per seam, not to rate welders.
Watching and correcting do not change.
unknowns: Whether the power sources can export data.

incremental.description: Welder selects the seam on the tablet before welding.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Work without recorded parameters has no paper to drop.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The welder keeps every judgement at the arc; binders and paper records move to the workstation tablet.
role.ambitious_version: A welder whose record of every seam is complete without writing a word.
